paper_metadata.title: Risk Factors of Ischemic and Hemorrhagic Stroke During Veno-Venous Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation: Analysis of Data from the Extracorporeal Life Support Organization Registry

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study uses a massive international registry (ELSO), which provides a large sample size. However, participation is voluntary, and the registry relies on ICD codes and voluntary reporting without central adjudication, which may lead to selection bias or under-reporting of the target population.

items.label: Source of target population
items.prompt: The source population or population of interest is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: Data reported to the Extracorporeal Life Support Organization by 366 ECMO centers from 2013 to 2019.
items.reasoning: The source is clearly defined as the ELSO registry, encompassing a global network of ECMO centers.

items.label: Method used to identify population
items.prompt: The sampling frame and recruitment are adequately described, including methods to identify the sample sufficient to limit potential bias (number and type used, e.g., referral patterns in health care)
items.evidence_snippet: The ELSO registry is a voluntary database that collects information on use, indications, complications, and outcomes of ECMO support in adults and children from 366 member centers worldwide.
items.reasoning: While the registry is described, the 'voluntary' nature of reporting introduces potential bias as not all eligible patients globally or within centers may be captured.

items.label: Recruitment period
items.prompt: Period of recruitment is adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: We carried out a retrospective analysis of the ELSO registry database from 2013 through 2019.
items.reasoning: The timeframe is explicitly stated.

items.label: Place of recruitment
items.prompt: Place of recruitment (setting and geographic location)  are adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: 366 ECMO centers from 2013 to 2019... member centers worldwide.
items.reasoning: The setting (ECMO centers) and global scope are described.

items.label: Inclusion and exclusion criteria
items.prompt: Inclusion and exclusion criteria are adequately described (e.g., including explicit diagnostic criteria or “zero time” description).
items.evidence_snippet: We included only patients 18 years and older who received one run of V-V ECMO support for respiratory failure. We excluded patients who underwent multiple runs... Patients treated with V-A ECMO were excluded.
items.reasoning: Criteria are clearly defined to isolate the V-V ECMO population.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study focuses on in-hospital outcomes (stroke and mortality) within a registry that tracks patients until discharge or death. Attrition is minimal in this acute setting, though some missing data for specific variables exists.

items.label: Proportion of baseline sample available for analysis
items.prompt: Response rate (i.e., proportion of study sample completing the study and providing outcome data) is adequate.
items.evidence_snippet: Overall in-hospital mortality was 36%... survival to hospital discharge.
items.reasoning: The registry tracks patients through their hospital stay; the primary outcomes (stroke/death) are recorded for the cohort.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: Prognostic factors (pre-ECMO and on-ECMO variables) are clearly defined, but the timing of measurement is limited to specific windows (e.g., 6 hours pre-cannulation), and there is missing data for several physiological variables.

items.label: Definition of the PF
items.prompt: A clear definition or description of 'PF' is provided (e.g., including dose, level, duration of exposure, and clear specification of the method of measurement).
items.evidence_snippet: The pre-extracorporeal life support (ECLS) hemodynamics and arterial blood gas (ABG) values were measured no more than 6 hours before initiation of ECLS
items.reasoning: The timing and nature of the prognostic factors (ABG, hemodynamics) are specified.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of PF
items.prompt: Method of PF measurement is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and limited reliance on recall).
items.evidence_snippet: ABG values were drawn between 18 and 30 hours after ECLS start time.
items.reasoning: Standard clinical laboratory measurements (ABG) are generally reliable.

items.reasoning: Standardized ELSO reporting forms ensure similar data collection across centers.

items.reasoning: There is significant missing data for some physiological variables (e.g., ~33% missing for MAP).

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The primary outcome (stroke) is likely under-reported. Diagnosis was not protocolized (no mandatory CT/MRI), and the registry relies on voluntary reporting without central adjudication. Autopsy data cited in the paper suggests the true incidence is much higher.

items.label: Definition of the Outcome
items.prompt: A clear definition of outcome is provided, including duration of follow-up and level and extent of the outcome construct.
items.evidence_snippet: ischemic stroke is defined as central nervous system (CNS) infarction determined by ultrasound, CT, or magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Hemorrhagic stroke is defined as intra- or extra-parenchymal CNS hemorrhage
items.reasoning: Definitions are provided based on imaging and clinical criteria.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Outcome
items.prompt: The method of outcome measurement used is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and confirmation of outcome with valid and reliable test).
items.evidence_snippet: ELSO data is reported voluntarily without central or local adjudication of neurological diagnoses, and CT scans of the brain were not mandated
items.reasoning: The lack of mandatory imaging and adjudication creates a high risk of misclassification and under-detection.

items.label: Method and Setting of Outcome Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of outcome measurement is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: it is unclear when and for which indications CT brain studies were performed
items.reasoning: While the registry is the same, the clinical practice (when to scan a patient) varied by center and patient.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The authors used multivariable logistic regression to adjust for several clinical confounders. However, critical data such as anticoagulation intensity (INR, aPTT) and the presence of Patent Foramen Ovale (PFO) were missing from the registry and could not be adjusted for.

items.label: Important Confounders Measured
items.prompt: All important confounders, including treatments (key variables in conceptual model: LIST), are measured.
items.evidence_snippet: the ELSO registry lacks several important explanatory variables... including anticoagulation data, occurrence of atrial fibrillation, patent foramen ovale, platelet counts
items.reasoning: Key clinical confounders related to stroke (anticoagulation, PFO) were not available.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The statistical methods are appropriate for the study design. The authors used multivariable logistic regression and reported odds ratios with confidence intervals. They also acknowledged the limitations of their data and the potential for underestimation.

items.label: Presentation of analytical strategy
items.prompt: There is sufficient presentation of data to assess the adequacy of the analysis.
items.evidence_snippet: Odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated by logistic regression analysis. Akaike information criterion was calculated for selecting the best model.
items.reasoning: The analytical strategy is well-described.

items.evidence_snippet: We carefully selected clinically relevant variables that had biologically plausible associations or causality
items.reasoning: Variable selection was based on clinical relevance and biological plausibility.

items.prompt: The selected statistical model is adequate for the design of the study.
items.evidence_snippet: multivariable logistic regression analysis to identify risk factors
items.reasoning: Logistic regression is appropriate for binary outcomes (stroke vs. no stroke).

items.label: Reporting of results
items.prompt: There is no selective reporting of results.
items.evidence_snippet: Results are expressed as the mean with standard deviation... or as the median with quartiles... All analyses were carried out in STATA 15.
items.reasoning: The authors report on all pre-specified outcomes (ischemic, hemorrhagic, brain death) and provide full tables of results.
